text: Sometimes you don't know how many arguments a function will get — that's exactly what star-args solves.
Put a single star before a parameter, and Python collects every extra positional argument into a tuple called numbers.
So sum_all works with five numbers, or two, or any count you throw at it.
[sniff] Double-star kwargs does the same for keyword arguments, gathering them into a dictionary.
Here print_info accepts any named values and loops over them as key-value pairs.
You can combine all three — regular parameters, star-args, and double-star kwargs — in a single function.
[chuckle] The order matters though: normal parameters first, then star-args, then double-star kwargs at the very end.
And the star works in reverse too — put a star before a list when calling, and Python unpacks it into separate arguments.
[groan] That unpacking trick is everywhere in real Python code, so it's well worth getting comfortable with it.
Up next, lambdas. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
